observations: Multiple white plastic (HDPE) containers enclosed in galvanized steel cages.
Stacked two-high in an outdoor or industrial yard.
Discharge valves are visible at the bottom center of the units in photo 1.
Metal identification plates are attached to the cages, but the text is illegible from this distance.
Units are mounted on integrated pallets, appearing to be a mix of metal and plastic/composite bases.

claims.claim: Storage drum for fluid or viscous materials.
claims.evidence: The photos show IBC tanks, which are the industry standard for transporting and storing bulk liquids and semi-solids.

risks.risk: Contamination from previous contents (e.g., toxic chemicals vs. food-grade).
risks.proof: A clear photo of the manufacturer's identification plate or the original product label showing previous contents.
risks.if_unproven: priced as non-food grade/chemical use only

risks.risk: Seized, leaking, or missing discharge valve components.
risks.proof: A close-up photo or video showing the valve handle moving and the internal seal intact.
risks.if_unproven: priced as having a faulty valve requiring replacement

risks.risk: Punctures or stress cracks in the plastic inner tank.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the bottom corners and the area around the valve.
risks.if_unproven: priced as having minor structural wear

proof_requests: Clear photo of the metal identification plate or any labels on the plastic tank.
Video of the discharge valve being opened and closed.
Confirmation of what was previously stored in these specific units.
response.reason: The items are clearly identifiable as standard 1000L IBC tanks. They can be priced at the baseline for used, unwashed containers with unknown history and unverified valve functionality.
